language.name: High Elven Court Speech
language.purpose: Original constructed language for formal Elven speech in Kael-Vossen.
design_rules: Vocabulary must be broad and genuinely varied rather than recycling a small set of fantasy syllables.
Canonical words must remain clearly distinct from ordinary English/Common vocabulary.
Romanization is the manuscript-facing representation; the native script is separately defined.
Meaning should remain understandable through context even when a reader does not know the language.
Formal court speech, military speech, casual speech, insults, and ritual language use distinct registers.
Existing manuscript meanings are preserved when the database expands the language.
Lyra learned the language from archival texts and treaties but never spoke it regularly; her fluency is therefore literary and rusty rather than native.

alphabet.name: Veyrath
alphabet.principle: A flowing angular script designed for inscription on living wood, crystal, metal, and ceremonial cloth.
alphabet.romanization: Latin characters are used only as a practical manuscript and translator representation until the native glyph set is finalized.
alphabet.note: Roman letters are not the in-world alphabet.

phonotactic_notes: Use varied roots, syllable lengths, and consonant clusters.
Avoid repeatedly building words from the same visible fragments.
Avoid accidental English/Common resemblance wherever a distinct form is possible.
Court forms may be longer and more precise; battlefield commands may be clipped.

grammar.default_word_order: verb-subject-object in formal declarations; flexible order in conversation
notes: Formal speech favors explicit titles and evidential precision.
Possession and rank use dedicated grammatical particles rather than English-style apostrophe construction.
Questions use interrogative particles and syntax rather than relying only on English word order.
Different registers may alter word order, contractions, and honorific usage.

vocabulary.meaning: exile; one cast beyond lawful belonging

translator.notes: Mappings are deliberately one-to-one where possible so the language can be implemented in a deterministic translator. New phrases should be added with grammatical analysis rather than invented ad hoc.

manuscript_usage.lyra: Literary competence with rusty spoken fluency. She may pause, search for an inflection, choose an overly formal construction, or correct herself when speaking.
manuscript_usage.commander: Native-level precision. His speech should reflect rank, military discipline, and contempt toward the Valerius bloodline.
manuscript_usage.citizens: Use shorter, colloquial forms and occasional idioms once the casual register is developed.
